newsitem.title: UK: UK finance directors give cautious budget welcome.
newsitem.headline: UK finance directors give cautious budget welcome.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's first budget has met with a cautious welcome from U.K. finance directors, a survey from Reed Accountancy Personnel/Accountancy Age magazine said on Thursday.
Forty-two percent of the 200 finance directors polled said they were happy with the July 2 budget, agreeing that the budget was good for their business.
They particularly welcomed the decrease in corporation tax and the increase in capital allowances for small businesses.

Thirty-two percent of finance directors felt that the budget had had an overall neutral effect on their businesses. Their main worry was that the abolition of advance corporation tax relief on pension funds would increase their costs.
"It's OK for fat overfunded pension schemes but punitive for those which are not," one finance director who was not named said.
There were also some doubts about the effectiveness of the budget at managing inflation with many finance directors expecting interest rates to rise shortly as a result.
There were fears that this would mean a further rise in sterling and another blow to Britain's competitiveness.

The Bank of England's monetary policy committee is due to announce its decision on interest rates at 1100 GMT. Most economists are expecting Britain's official 6.5 percent interest rates to rise to 6.75 percent.
